html:
The Brihadisvara Temple is a great Hindu temple to Shiva in Thanjavur, south India, built by the Chola king Rajaraja I and finished in 1010.

It is one of the largest temples of its age anywhere. Its tower over the shrine rises about 66 metres in tiers of granite, topped by a single huge capstone. Granite had to be hauled in from quarries far away, as there is none near Thanjavur. It is a model of Dravidian architecture, where the tower over the god, not the gateway, is the tallest part.

The walls carry long inscriptions. They record Rajaraja's gifts of gold, land and villages, and name the hundreds of people the temple paid: dancers, musicians, priests, accountants, lamp keepers. The temple was a bank, a landlord and an employer as well as a shrine.

His son built a rival at Gangaikonda Cholapuram. Both are part of the World Heritage Site of the Great Living Chola Temples, and Brihadisvara is still in worship today.
sum: The Brihadisvara Temple is a great Hindu temple to Shiva in Thanjavur, south India, built by the Chola king Rajaraja I and finished in 1010.
